newsitem.title: USA: Georgia task force recommends gas tax hike - paper.
newsitem.headline: Georgia task force recommends gas tax hike - paper.

text.p: A Georgia transportation task force has proposed doubling the state's gasoline tax to pay for rural highways and cleaning up urban air quality, the Atlanta Journal Constitution said.
The proposal would raise the tax to 15 cents per gallon, from 7.5 cents.

The task force of local government, business and transportation officials and environmental experts was appointed by the state Department of Transportation. It will formally present its recommendation to the board on Dec 19.
Under the plan, half of the new revenues would be directed toward the governor's Road Improvement Program, a system of 13 developmental highways in rural Georgia.

Two cents of the increase would be used to pay off escalating debt service on that program, which will exceed $130 million next year. Another two cents would be used to pay for new construction on the system.
The remaining new money would be split between local road projects and mass transit in urban areas.

The plan also calls for a special tax for the 13-county Atlanta metropolitan area, possibly an emmissions testing surcharge or added vehicle registration fee, to pay for air quality improvement projects.

The plan faces several hurdles. The state constitution restricts gasoline tax spending to roads and bridges. Any spending for other transportation modes would require approval from voters, who rejected a similar amendment in 1992.
Additionally, Gov. Zell Miller said he remains opposed to any tax increase, and would not sign one into law.
